text: I went to Bistro St. Tropez for Valentine's Day, 2015. The location is on the river, however unfortunately the room we were in where the bar is) had windows that were fogged over, so that diminished the ambiance a bit. Our server was very attentive and had a great personality. As many restaurants do for Valentine's day, Mother's Day, and the like, the menu was a "special" pre-fixe at $68. This included an amuse of a lobster tart, a starter (I had the foie gras), a main (I had the rack of lamb), and a shared dessert. My date had a salad as her starter and scallops as her main. To say that the $68 price tag for the "special" menu was overpriced is an understatement. The amuse was amuse-sized; my foie gras was just as small as the amuse, and two average bites at best. The entree was a nicely prepared rack of frenched lamb chops, "lollipop" sized, and the dessert was probably 1.25 the size of a dessert for one person. I also added an extra course of oysters; 6 for $14, which was actually a reasonable price for six very nice pieces. Everything we had was good, but certainly not outstanding, but it's the ridiculous pricing that really upset me. The "special" menu was (as accurately as I can tell) just about 100% more expensive than the usual three-course menu. I can understand a premium for a "special" day, but I think the restaurant really took advantage of its diners on this particular day. Overall, the value for the price was substantially below my expectations, and while I had a nice time with my date, I left with a very bad opinion of the restaurant. I really don't know if I'd return for this reason alone.

text: A rather inconspicuous dining option in the El Dorado Resort and the oh so dim "romantic" lighting at 6 pm on a Sunday didn't warrant attention from passerby(s) either. However, I must say that I was extremely pleased with my dining experience, the food was exceptional & the service was even better. I ordered the mushroom ravioli, hands down by far the best I've ever had. Explosion of flavor and just the right texture with the perfect amount of sauce. My boyfriend ordered the boneless half chicken mattone (quite a substantial amount of food- no skimping here whatsoever). The skin was roasted and seasoned to perfection, the chicken itself was moist- always a plus. It was served with roasted potatoes and broccolinis with a house lemon mustard dressing. Usually I'm not a fan of chicken because they're always either too dry or lacking in flavor. Kudos to La Strada for getting this dish down to a science, everything complemented each other. However, what blew my mind was the free bread that was served as starters. Make no mistake, these were no ordinary bread. Had I not known better, I'd swear they were laced with something. 4 different types of bread arrived at our table before the meal, all pipin hot & fresh out the oven- the bread sticks and garlic bread were to die for. No joke, both of us would've been solely satisfied just off the bread. Tip: ease off the bread so you can relish in your main dish. Our server let us know that most patrons ask & are allowed to take the bread home.

text: Superb ambience, food, customer service. Wow, where do I begin? No other restaurant have been deserving of a second review, but Musashi is so amazing in every aspects that it blown my mind and blew all other restaurants out of the water. First, the moment I stepped in, Keiko-san instantly recognized me and welcomed me back even though the last time I visited was about two months ago. Keiko-san was just as friendly, polite, and helpful as she was when this place first opened. Secondly, the food is still fantastic. The ramen noodle is springy, the broth is rich and creamy, and the nitamago (marinated egg) is creamy on the inside and savory. We ordered the Musashi Sampler filled with dim sum, shui mai, curry beef and chicken, and gyoza for $12 which was excellent. My family ordered the Unagi (Eel) Rice Bowl and the deep caramel colored eel was a melt-in-your-mouth sensation, I have always been wary of bones in the eel but there were none here! Also, the salmon and tuna nigiri are amazingly fresh. The salmon has a vibrant orange and white color and tastes rich and buttery. The tuna is red as a rose and has no gristle. Lastly, we finished with the green tea creme brulee and ani tofu (almond tofu). The almond tofu dessert has fruits, almond tofu, and green tea agar tofu, both are fantastic and the agar jelly is light, milky, and slightly sweet with a fragrant almond aftertaste. The green tea creme brulee was subtly sweet with the hidden bitterness of the green tea. The brown sugar crust was crunchy, sweet, and smokey. It was a sweet finale to the meal. I am definitely planning to visit again.

text: I was really excited about this place because I hate cooking, and I like to eat foods that are more natural. Sadly, though, I couldn't have been any more disappointed in Fitlife. And we're not talking fancy meals here ... just very plain meals that you could make at home with little to no culinary skill for a fraction of the price that Fitlife charges. On a related note, I see many people argue that organic food is costly. True. But even for organic food, Fitlife is too expensive. AND where is the proof that the meals are organic? I see nothing on Fitlife's website or menu to indicate that their food is organic. They use terms to make you think it's really "natural," but anyone can make that claim. Unless it's certified organic, they could be feeding you any line of crap and you'd just have to take their word for it. Additionally, the meals aren't even very good. I'm not hard to please when it comes to food. But one of the meals I had was mediocre to bad, and the another was one of the worst meals i've ever had. Not even remotely acceptable for $12-$13 a piece. Finally, the majority of the food has hot pepper in it. I looked through their meals one-by-one and tried to find something that didn't have hot pepper, and I could barely find any. Their CHICKEN ALFREDO has cayenne pepper. Seriously?! They probably make it spicy to try to cover up the fact that the meals taste terrible. Oh, and I've heard them say their containers are BPA free, like that's a big perk. Most plastic food containers are now BPA free ... that's nothing to brag about. This feels like one of those places that knows if they use generic terms like "!00% natural," then they can convince you that it's healthy and make a large profit. I mean, what does "100% natural" even really mean? It's all marketing strategy. Fitlife sounds great in theory, but the reality is much different. Despite what they claim, Fitlife is not about selling quality products and making your life easier -- they are about selling hype and a false image. Be smart and think critically -- don't get sucked into their trap. Save your money and shop elsewhere.

Every time I would walk in no one would say hello- it was just handing over my pup on her leash and that was it. Anytime I had a question it was like a bother to them for me to ask. If they treat the people who pay that way- how do they treat our dogs while we aren't there?? Our pup was not big on eating first thing in the morning before we left the house so I gave them food for my dog to eat for the late morning/early afternoon when she was often hungry. All too often they would have the same container of dog food still full or mostly all of it still left by the end of the week. They clearly weren't giving our baby any of the food I had requested them too. She would come home ravaging and would gobble up her dinner within 5 mins. The final straw was when I went to pick up our baby after work and Michelle told me it would be a good idea to have her put down!! WHAT?!? They claimed that she had tried to bite at one of the helper girls while they tried to get her leash off. That place has new girls helping out there all the time and our dog was not an aggressive girl. The girl who tried to take her leash off probably startled her a bit or did something to make our pup feel uncomfy but by no means is that a cause to tell someone to put their dog down. Our dog has never hurt a soul. Needless to say I was shocked and began to cry. Rather than giving me a hug or saying something to try to make me feel better, Michelle stayed stone cold and just said that I could always get another. EXCUSE ME?!? The worst part was that she didn't even take me into a back office or make our conversation private- instead she said it right at the front door in front of everyone. How professional is that?? That is when I took my pup and ran and never returned. There is not a chance in hell that I'd ever recommend this place to anyone who truly loves their dog. These owners need lessons in manners, customer care and professionalism. Awful and disgraceful.
label: NEG

text: The rating is not a reflection on their food but their terrible service! I am on a low carb diet- I order their wings at least once a week and always ask for "all drums" because I feel you get more meat than the flats. Before I get into the review, I would like to say the only reason it is not 1 star is because their drivers are ALL awesome! They are fast, courteous, very professional and always get all of the sauces I request. But that is where it 100% stops. The person who answers their phones is one of the rudest employees I have ever come across. Normally I let it slide but last night took it to a whole new level. They have messed up my order on 3 different occasions, once giving me bbq wings, and twice giving me all flats, so when I placed my normal order last night, I asked her to read me back to confirm the order. When she didn't say "all drums" I politely said "please don't forget I am asking for all drums, I hate saying that but it was wrong last time and I really don't want to have to send the driver back". This is where she RAISED her voice and said "MA'AM you are going to get all DRUMS" and then HUNG UP ON ME. Whoa. So I did what any normal person would do, I called back to ask for their manager. After 4 minutes on hold, the manager is the one who answered the phone, I introduced myself as one of their weekly regular customers and told her exactly what happened. Instead of apologizing- she deflected and said "you may not get all drums because we have to pick through the frozen batch to get the drums out of each batch in their package" and then proceeded to keep talking about their prep process and my order rather than focusing on how their employees treat their customers. I calmly said "ma'am, I understand the drum situation but what I am upset about is the fact that your employee raised her voice at me and hung up!" She did not even acknowledge what I had just said- instead going back to the drums. Finally, I said "ma'am- you are the manager of this place, I do not care about the wings at this point and I am telling you that I am hugely aggravated by the way your employee cocked an attitude with me and then hung up, can we address this please". Long silence. She finally responds "yes ma'am, I'll talk to her, is that all?". Wow. No apology, no nothing. If I didn't really love their wings, I would be through with this place.

Only 4 cheese curds in the entire box and the fries were clearly previously frozen. The gravy was flavorless. Not about to let a flavorless poutine stop us from what was supposed to be flavor heaven, we continued on to order meals. My husband ordered the Blue Pig grilled cheese. This was basically blueberry jam toast... overflowing with blueberry jam, only 2 slices of bacon on the entire sandwich, and the cheese was nonexistent ($10!). His side of chili tasted canned and not fresh made. I had the chicken sausage with blue cheese and wing sauce, because I'll eat wing sauce and blue cheese on just about anything. Again, this was uninspired. The description was accurate, it was a chicken sausage with blue cheese, drizzled with wing sauce. It was fine, nothing to come back for. Side of bacon mac salad was pasta and mayonnaise, with a tiny bacon-bit. Overall, the restaurant we have been dying to try, and were so excited to have finally opened, was disappointing. I might beg to go back for a milkshake, but with Bodega and Red Mesa Mercado down the street, it is going to be a tough sell.

text: This is my new obsession. Like our Yelp Tampa CM Brett I have an unchained infatuation with frozen sugar. The day after my first visit to Jeremiah's it was the first thing I thought of when I woke up. (Yes I know I have a problem.) I've enjoyed other Italian ice before but this is just so far beyond everything else I've tried. With Italian ice I'm used to fruit flavors, such as lemon. When you first look at the (huge) list of available flavors several of them don't make sense. Chocolate? How can they have chocolate Italian ice? They do and it's awesome. I don't think anyone would disagree that chocolate mint is the best ice cream flavor of all time, but as Italian ice? Believe me it works, even with the included bits of chocolate to crunch. When you make your selection you can do three different things. You could decide to only get soft serve ice cream. Note: you might be crazy if you do this. You could just get Italian ice and combine flavors if you want. The third option is to get a gelati, which is Italian ice and soft serve together. All of the other places I've been to either slap the ice cream on top or blend it like a milkshake. Jeremiah's puts some ice on the bottom, a layer of soft serve, another layer of ice (maybe a different flavor), more soft serve, another layer of ice, and more soft serve. It's madness! So far the scoop froggy frog (chocolate mint) is my favorite. I also made a creation that was part cookies and cream and part salted caramel with chocolate ice cream. I think next time I'm going to try a chocolate and peanut butter creation. The seating area reminds me of a middle school cafeteria. You're going here for the treats though, not the ambience. Sign up for their email list and you'll get some free ice once in a while. If Jeremiah's ever leaves Tampa I am going to have a week of mourning.
label: POS

text: I'm not the biggest fan of going to a restaurant to cook your own food. Having your food cooked in front of you? Awesome. It's hard for me to say what I put in my bowl because I put a little of everything. Mostly chicken and seafood with a little steak. For my vegetables I did mostly just peppers and onions but they have an array of fresh veggies for you to select what you want. Then you choose your seasonings then you choose a sauce. Or mix your own sauce like I did. From what I saw of some of the other guests you can pile your bowl as high as you like with the raw stuff and once they cook it on super high heat it will cure all of the issues you might have with your food touching. Maybe that's just me. Make sure you're pretty liberal with the the seasonings and the sauces and your food will turn out good. I really loved the teryaki sauce and then they have a dragon salt seasoning that's amazing. Once you take your bowl to the chef, you choose your starches and the chef will prepare your bowl and someone brings it to your table. The bread bowl was tasty, too, and I liked that it wasn't as tough as some of the bowls I've had in the past from other places. My husband, who loves your standard white bread, actually really liked both breads. More recently, I ordered their cinnamon roll for Christmas breakfast. The cinnamon roll comes as one large roll of raw dough, to be cut into 10 cinnamon buns and baked, and is frozen until ready to use. It also comes with a tub of frosting. The cinnamon roll was rather pricey (somewhere in the $33 range, if I recall correctly), but it was really good. I would consider making this a Christmas tradition. text: I am giving this place a higher rating than the taste quality of their food which I'd rank a "3" of 5 stars. They do too many other things right not to acknowledge their "right track". The place is a British style gastropub set in an old farmhouse that's been around since at least the early 1900s (one said 1890). It has been other restaurants as well as an orphanage and a farmhouse. It has a beautiful southern veranda and brick "bones", with tasteful décor. It's warm and inviting. Great ambiance. The veranda has plastic shades that help with the heat on cool winter days. The help is enthusiastic, knowledgeable and helpful. We were seated and served quickly and accommodated when we desired to move inside for warmth. The craft beer menu is many pages, including a non-alcoholic Guinness that I found delicious ($4.50 though). There are inside and outside bars. The bathroom is outside. They have a ramp access for those who need it. There's a pool table. They have special music programs scheduled. Their menu is well thought out, their portions are large. The disappointment was in the lacks in flavor of their well-plated and appetizing food items. The chicken salad sandwich was thick and ground fine. We wished for more flavor, such as pickle or paprika or celery. The tomato-basil soup looked beautiful and was piping hot, but had no depth and a grainy texture. The spinach salad was bright & healthy looking but the "warm dressing" had too thick a layer of oil on top that wouldn't mix in and the "flavored lumps" seemed more like wet artificial bacon bits-the balsamic used was not a good tart balance for the mixture. The prices were excellent--$6 for soup and sandwich for example. Our highpoint was the salted caramel cheesecake. TEN stars. Best we've ever had. Went straight to the top of our favorite desserts list. This alone would be a reason to return. Soooo our mixed review is very high overall but lowered by the flavorless but pretty entrees.
label: POS

text: I'm writing this review after regularly eating at El Limon's other branches (Ardmore and Conshohocken). I live in Haverford, so I'm essentially between Ardmore and Bryn Mawr; Typically I go to the Ardmore location, since the parking situation is a bit better. Ardmore and Conshohocken are always great- service is quick and accurate and the food is out of the kitchen pretty quickly, even on busy nights. The portions are hearty sized, visually appealing and delicious. Execution at both locations are virtually identical and always consistent. I figured Bryn Mawr would be the same. Alas, this was not the case. What were the issues? 1) Service. In the time I'm usually seated, ordered and served at the other locations, the wait staff had not yet even taken my order for a drink. For context of the crowd, the restaurant was barely half full. 2) Execution. After waiting a substantial amount of time for service and ordering the food, when it came out, it was executed poorly. The tacos were all over the plate (not stacked side-by-side) and the toppings were uneven and/or not even in the taco (there was more onion and cilantro on the plate than on the tacos). 3) Taste. I ordered steak, al pastor and chorizo tacos. All were burnt. I don't mean scorched. I mean, charred and blackened through and through. 4) Consistency. So the service was off, execution and taste were off. Portion sizes were noticeably smaller and the wait staff were either running around with the illusion of being busy, or in the back by the kitchen yelling at each other. Overall, I really want El Limon to do well in Bryn Mawr. They have a solid menu with great food at an unbeatable price. That said, Bryn Mawr may have been one branch too far. After seeing perfect consistency and execution at the other locations, I know it's not impossible to expect it throughout all the branches. After my experience there, I will only recommend Ardmore and Conshohocken locations.

text: PROS: -Neat, clean restaurant -Price - while not the cheapest taqueria, still good prices -Friendly staff CONS: -rather bland flavors and odd food combinations LOCATION: Small strip center on the corner of Columbus and Lincoln. Parking is available in front and on the side. FOOD: The menu provides a good range of traditional Mexican items. Tacos make up about a quarter of the choices. They can be ordered individually ($1.49) or as part of a platter (up to $8). Protein choices include: asada, pastor, barbacoa, carnitas, chick and fish. A good chunk of the menu is focused on Mexican meals such as enchiladas, bistec and fajitas. Prices range from $8 - $14. There are also a number of a la cart-type options including burritos, quesadillas and flautas in the $8- $10 range. On my visit, I had a cup of tortilla soup and a burrito with carnitas. While simple, the soup was very good. Unfortunately, the burrito was a real disappointed - on a couple of levels. First, the carnita meat was tender and juicy but very light on flavor. It was as if it was well stewed but with very little seasonings. Second, the guts of thing included "pickled" jalapenos. I have nothing against jalapenos, I love them. But, as a Mexican restaurant, use fresh ones if you are going to use them in your food! I also think there was mayo involved - gack. The most obnoxious part was the pile of ruffled french fries served with it. Really? Fries instead of beans and rice or at least something that goes with the style? If quantity of food is important, both the burrito and the pile of fries were large portions. I was pretty underwhelmed with my food but it wasn't horrible, 2 Stars for Food. SERVICE: I sat at the bar and my waitress was excellent. There was a bit of a language barrier but she was polite and friendly. On my lunch visit, there were about 15 patrons who kept both servers busy. However, service was timely and without issues. I have no problem giving 5 stars for Service. VALUE: Overall, I'd say menu prices are a bit higher than average but you do get a lot of food. However, I didn't particularly enjoy my burrito and really didn't eat the fries. They do have a daily special (it was a $5.99 quesadilla the day I was there) and half-priced beer from 2 - 6 Monday - Thursday. I'll give 3 stars for Value. ATMOSPHERE: The interior is a touch divey with a gaudy red bar but its airy and clean. Several nice tv's are mounted around the place playing ESPN and soccer (futbol). I actually like the atmosphere. 4 stars for Atmosphere. Overall, I'm not writing this place off because I do want to try the tacos. I'm kicking myself for not doing that on this visit. I'll update this review once I do! Food: 6/10, Service: 9/10, Value: 7/10, Atmosphere 7/10

text: OK Yelp reader - repeat after me - "I am going to come to the Palace Cafe and eat the crab cheesecake!" Say it again.... and again... then go do it. Yes it's that good, that no trip to New Orleans is complete without it. 5+++++ stars and is truly one of the greatest things I've eaten in my life. Those that know my yelp reviews, know that I don't make such statements lightly. It's only $9.50 and listed as an appetizer. It's on their breakfast, brunch, lunch, and dinner menu. It's their signature dish, so you have no excuse not get it. You don't have a large dining budget you say? No problem, don't have a whole meal at the Palace Cafe, just order a slice of the crab cheesecake and sit at an outside table. The point is, however you do it, get it, eat it, thank me later. We came here for a Sunday Jazz Brunch at Noon. I'm torn on if I should rate the Palace Cafe 4 stars or 5 stars. If I'm rating the whole entire jazz brunch experience, then it's 5 stars. What's not to love a jazz trio (clarinet, banjo, and upright bass) playing classic New Orleans standards. Sometimes they are moving from table to table, other times they are hanging out on the stairwell landing, playing down to the customers below. We did the make your own bloody mary, which can be a good thing or a bad thing, depending on how well you know what you are doing. They have many infused vodkas to choose from. I recommend the bacon infused vodka. There are also some really tasty marinated mushrooms to put in there. It's easy to over do it though with all the add in options available to you, so be careful. We started off with some charcuterie - The Petite Campagne, which consisted of prosciutto, lamb terrine, country pate, venison salami, and duck rillettes. Everything was absolutely delicious. The duck rillettes to me answered the question - What if you made chicken salad out of duck? The answer was "you'd have something way better". A little of this on some crunchy bread and we were off to a good start. The pate and terrine, went well with various pickled veggies and chutney. There were also a couple of nice mustards for the salami and prosciutto. 5 stars Our waiter was smart to hold off on placing the rest of our order so we never felt rushed while enjoying our charcuterie, after all the Place Cafe is what you are here to do. Take in your surroundings and enjoy a leisurely meal. Too many negative reviews about this place involve "It took too long and I had somewhere else to be, so service was bad" Next up was the Crabmeat Cheesecake. My brother made sure we each ordered our own, which I was surprised. We usually share so we can order more things, but he has had the crab cheesecake before and knew how divine it is. He was right from the first bite, I wouldn't have wanted to share this, and would have protected it like Smeagol and his ring. In fact they should change the name of this dish to "My Precious". It's almost quiche like in consistency with a pecan crust. The filling is a rich mixture of mostly shredded crab, caramelized onions, and cream cheese. Topped off with sautéed wild mushrooms and a brown creole meuniere sauce. The sauce is so good, I made sure there wasn't a drop left by mopping up any leftovers with a piece of bread. If that's not enough, on top of the cheese cake there are 3 lightly breaded small crab claws with most of the shell removed. Now those are my kind of lollipops! 6 stars Perhaps the Palace Cafe was a victim of it's own success at this point. With the Crabmeat Cheesecake being so mind blowing, there was nowhere to go but down. We shared two main dishes. Our waiter paid attention that we said we were sharing, and actually had them plate two smaller versions of each dish, separately. It was unexpected and extremely nice of him to do so. I'm not sure if the extra plating time lead to lukewarm food, but that was the result unfortunately. Braised Beef Short Rib Benedict - red wine braised beef short ribs, poached eggs, stone ground grits, sautéed spinach, Béarnaise sauce, Bordelaise sauce. The egg was cooked perfectly and the yolk exploded when I poked into it. The grits, I found a little bit on the tasteless side, which was a shame. I found myself wishing this dish was constructed on a toasted muffin, to add some texture. 3.5 stars Cafe Eggs Benedict - Pork "Debris", cheddar biscuit, poached eggs, and tasso Hollandaise. Again a perfectly cooked poached egg, although not very hot. This combination sounded better than it turned out to be, and was just ok. 3 stars. Table side Bananas Foster - While this makes a great show, doing it table side, doesn't allow enough time for the bananas to get caramelized nice and sticky. 3.5 stars White Chocolate Bread Pudding - This was outstanding and our waiter recommended a shot of El Dorado 15 year old rum to pour over it. Great call, the vanilla flavor of the rum really went perfectly with it. 5 Stars. Check out my photos.

The restaurant also has a full bar that serves mixed cocktails, craft beers on tap, wine, and sake! The staff are fun and friendly and love to chat. text: My fiancé and I hired Best to perform the termite inspection of the home he purchased for the loan. In May, three weeks after closing, I noticed a large bubble in the paint at the bottom of our front door jam. I poked the bubble and a ton of droppings poured out. As the area damaged by the termites seemed much too large to have appeared since the inspection, we contacted Best to inspect again, hoping they would determine they'd made a mistake and help correct the situation. Unfortunately, Best told us the damage was new and was not there at the time of the March inspection, and there was nothing they would do. With the exception of performing remediation at full price. As we were skeptical, we contacted another termite company who inspected and advised that the damage was certainly there at the time of the inspection, and that the area damaged should have been the very first place they should check for termites. Best's deficient termite inspection has cost us thousands of dollars and they've refused to help, or at the very least, refund their fee for the failed inspection. TL;DR Hired Best to perform our termite inspection when purchasing our home. text: Cat Hair Day loves to go out on dates. Nat is vegan, so we are limited to where we can go out to, but that's part of the fun - finding vegan-friendly places to eat in Indy. And trust us, we don't starve! We seem to find ourselves at the Sinking Ship on a weekly basis for a couple of reasons, it is right down the street and we love their wings! The Sinking Ship is located in SoBro at 49th and College. While it is known for being the only hockey bar in Indy, they also serve lunch and dinner, and even have a Sunday brunch. We were excited to find out on our most recent visit to the Sinking Ship, that they had just unveiled a new menu with even more vegan options! One of the greatest perks of The Sinking Ship, is that it is one of the more vegan-friendly restaurants we have found in Indy, with nearly half of the menu options being vegan. Unlike many restaurants, where you have to "special order" non-vegan options to make them vegan, The Sinking Ship has many options that are already vegan. Vegan options at The Sinking Ship include appetizers, sides, entrees, and burgers. Our favorite appetizers are the Sack of Balls (cinnamon sugar donut balls with a fruity sauce) and Vegan Chili Dogs. Our favorite go-to entree is their Seitan Wings with Korean BBQ; try them - we promise you won't regret it! The Thai Seitan Salad is another delicious lunch or dinner option, and one of the healthier menu items. Their vegan sides include Mac N' Teese and Vegan Chili. Another option worth mentioning is their variety of vegan sauces, including vegan ranch and vegan mayo. But the best day of all to visit the Sinking Ship is on Sundays when they have Vegan Biscuits and Gravy. We could eat their biscuits and gravy every week and never get tired of them. Seriously, they are so delicious! Time to Rate Vegan Friendly: 4/5 -almost half of the menu is vegan, including appetizers, entrees, burgers, sides, and special vegan sauces -they just unveiled a new menu with even more vegan options than before Tastiness: 3.5/5 -food is very hit or miss -the hits are chart topping, you think about them when you're at home and hungry and you then start to salivate -misses are just okay... not inedible, just nothing to blog about Decor: 4.5/5 (Nat); 4/5 (Amy) -considering it's a bar, the decorations are above average, including some pretty cool paintings on the walls -the bar is hockey themed, which is evident in the decor -there is a juke box, but it does not play music unless a guest has paid for songs, so it goes from being really loud for a few minutes to no music at all at times Staff Friendliness: 5/5 -the staff is friendly and the food comes fast, so you see them often Cost: $$ -priced well for the amount of food you get - most of the appetizers and entrees are under $10 Overall Feeling: 4/5 -we get excited about going there to get the food we love, but are wary of trying new things because they are either excellent or just ok; we never really know if we are going to like something until we try it -we understand that it is a bar but due to the acoustics it can get loud really fast, so it can be difficult to comfortably have a conversation Overall Rating: 4/5 -even more vegan options than before -fast and friendly service -very limited parking -no bike rack nearby -food inconsistency, with a few favorite items that we love and other options that we wouldn't try again Amy+Nat Cat Hair Day Cathairday.com

First, we were trying to book spa treatments prior to our arrival. Unfortunately, we were never able to just call and have someone answer. The message was "due to high call volume..." What is this; an insurance company hotline? We finally were able to get ahold of someone, and booked our treatments. When we arrived, the hotel entrance was very attractive, but not 4-5 star attractive. The front desk was very cordial and quickly sent us off to our room. When we walked in the room, it certainly looked acceptable, but not luxurious at all. As a matter of fact, the décor was rather hodgepodge. Some of the items which were supposed to be there were not, such as a bottle of wine and bottled water. The floors were dirty, there was hair in the bathtub, the chair cushions were stained, and refrigerator handle was broken. I didn't notice it, but my wife said the base of the toilet was dirty. Heck, we are usually supplied with a writing pen, but had none. When we walked to the beach, we quickly noticed it's didn't seem clean. However, there is a disclosure upon entry the beach seeps natural tar. That is on top of the oil rigs being very close to shore. Throughout the course of the weekend stay, there were certainly details I noticed which lacked a 4-5 star experience. The food from the Spa Café and in-room dining were expensive and bland. When I was looking for another eatery, the attendant at the Spa Café directed me to another location on the campus which turned out to be under renovation (what!? Employees don't know these things?). We had also left our tray from room service outside of our door around 10:30PM, and by the next day when we were checking out around 11:30AM, it was still there. Other annoyances were grounds employees with facial piercings and the cook from the Spa Café having a personal conversation on the front phone while I was waiting for my take-out food. This actually made me chuckle a bit, but I was coming back from a dinner around 9:30 PM and was holding a lot of stuff. I never experienced it, but supossedly the golf carts will haul you around the grounds. With all this stuff in my arms, a golf cart driver passed me right up and asked the couple in front of me if they needed a lift. HAHAHAHAHA!!!! Oh, man... The last straw which made us want to return home immediately was the spa service. My massage was below par for a whopping $160 + 20% gratuity, not to mentioned tried to be up sold on services right before the session. Who really wants to be up sold right before a so called world class massage. However, it's my wife's pedicure which really ticked me off. She had an appointment for a French pedicure. However they had mistakenly booked a mani/pedi combo. When my wife brought it to their attention, they said "okay" but we will leave it as is since you are not paying for it (my company was). The attendant even told the woman doing the nails to "leave it as a mani/pedi". My wife found that unethical and made them change it to only a pedicure and provide a receipt. When she returned to the room, she was so upset because her pedicure was terrible. The clear coat was gooped on, and there was a pink/red bleed on her white tips (where did the red come from?!). She immediately removed it when we arrived home. I'm usually the one to say, "Honey, it looks okay", but I must admit it was a very sloppy job for a $117 price tag, heck for a $30 price tag. Anyhow, there were some discrepancies at the front desk regarding the billing, but the front desk attendant, Anthony, was helpful and the disputed charges were sent to "investigate". I'm a bit perplexed by the Yelpers who give it a 5-star rating. I firmly believe if you have visited a 5 star resort, there is no way you can consider Bacara to be one. The experience was sub-par, and it would have been acceptable for a 3 star hotel, but there is no way I could recommend it or ever return. It appears these issues have been going on for years with no one to seriously address them. The GM responds on Yelp, but it seems to be the same boilerplate apology she has given the hundreds of other poor reviews. Do I see Hotel Rescue in the future? Edit: I just lowered it to one star because I realized the incidentals discrepancy which was supposed to be taken of by the front desk, but the way they took care of it was charging the amount to the card I told them not to charge! Arrrrrhhhh...I just want to forget all about Bacara, but they keep haunting me!
label: NEG

There was a man on the other end, asking if I had called his laundromat today and did I have a white hat? I immediately recognized the man's voice from the laundromat, and said I had. He said he was cleaning the machines for the night, when he found a load of laundry. I immediately realised I'd forgotten that one load in the washer. He said he'd dry them for me and I could pick up in the morning. When I got there in the morning, his wife was there folding clothing and gave me a beautiful smile. He explained that when he found my clothes, he knew I'd been the last to use that machine. So he went through his phone to see if he could find my number on it. They were such nice people that this is definitely the place in going to use in the future when I have a washing machine break down.

Before the facial began, I noted that I wanted less freckles from the sun, Cara recommended vitamin C, and I'm pretty sure I smelled something citrusy, generously applied to my face. text: I wasn't planning on dining at Seasons 52, a modestly sized national chain owned by Darden Restaurants emphasizing a menu that changes seasonally and offers fresher, healthier ingredients with all entrees said to have fewer than 475 calories. They also are known for offering an extensive, international wine list. All the featured items on the right side of their menu change on a weekly basis. I was pretty sure I was dressed too casually and I sensed a little hesitation as I wheeled into the Keystone Crossing location of Seasons 52. I was a little disheveled, but not sloppy. I was a little unkempt, but not truly messy. I certainly wasn't the only one dressed casually, but I'll admit I felt under-dressed the minute I entered their beautifully decorated entryway with warm woods, a meditative fountain at the entry way, atmosphere-setting lighting, and uniformly dressed employers whom all radiate a sense of calm and casual warmth. Truth be told, I arrived in Seasons 52 hoping for a friendly face and a good meal. While I'd put Seasons 52 on the lower end of finer dining, I was fully prepared to spoil myself a bit and wanting to eat a healthier meal. The other truth is that, for whatever reason, Father's Day for me this year was a bit more melancholy than usual. My daughter passed away years ago and I seldom observe the "day," preferring to simply not worry about it. Today, I wanted to observe it with a special meal and a sense of remembering. The hesitation I sensed, while partly my own, was also from a hostess whom I'm sure looked at me and kind of wondered if I'd stumbled into the right restaurant. Fortunately, she didn't flinch at all and, in fact, had another employee prepare a table and made sure she moved the chair. It was kind of a nice touch to have it moved before I arrived at the table. The restaurant was busy but not full and it seemed like most of the diners were with fathers and grandfathers celebrating the day together. I was pleasantly surprised to not be taken to an isolated two-top in the corner, but offered a four-top table in a decent location. The menu tends to consist of healthier fare, of course, so don't plan on ordering a burger & fries here. I opted for a roast chicken selection with spring vegetables, Yukon Gold mash, and herb-lemon sauce for $16.95. It seemed like most of the entrees were priced in the $15 - 25 range with appetizers and salads available in the $7-10 range. I also ordered my usual unsweetened iced tea and it was refilled twice, once without my asking and once as a way of determining if I was finishing up or lingering a bit. My entire bill ran about $21+ without tip. You can easily eat within this range, though it's also easy to add salads, appetizers, and/or dessert and have the price add up. Seasons 52 does offer a "Happy Hour Menu" from 4pm - 6:30pm on Monday - Friday that offers smaller plates of popular menu items for $5. It's a great way to give the place a try, though I have yet to try it out. For whatever reason, I was really feeling melancholy from Father's Day today and really appreciated the quality customer service despite showing up a bit under-dressed and unkempt. I felt a wee bit out of place, but was not made to feel "out of place" by the staff. I needed kindness today and that's what I got from the staff including server Tammy, whose friendliness fit the atmosphere yet also felt warm and sincere. The food was good with both a delicious taste and decent serving size. It was "healthy," but you also felt like you were getting a true meal. In a restaurant, that's not always an easy balance and this definitely worked. Sometimes, a little kindness makes all the difference in the world. Today, I got that plus a quality meal from the folks at Seasons 52. When I show up again, and I will, I'll likely dress up just a bit more but really appreciated that on a day when a little human connection was needed I was able to come in "as is" and be welcomed and treated well.
label: POS

The Red Sauce is great for anyone. 2, When you meet Antonio the owner/cook and talk to him about his food, you can tell he wouldn't compromise on ingredients, he takes a lot of pride in his traditional meals and gets excited when others enjoy it. Like any good chef, when we gave him our compliments, he was ear to ear smiles. 3, We leaned over the ordering counter and asked him what the gigantic pot (so big it took up most of the stove) was. He said, I'm already starting the food for tomorrow. Seeing the beautiful food steaming and simmering over the hot stove meant only one thing. We are coming back! We were so disappointed that we had no more room in our stomachs to try the other meals. When we got the bill, my boyfriend chuckled and said this is our new spot and we can afford to eat out several nights a week here. What a gem, crazy good food, friendly owner and it was cheap! This place is only going to grow in popularity and as it does, we hope Antonio keeps his reasonable prices - it just means we'll be seeing him more often. Tips: -Come hungry and you'll be glad you did. -Pulled pork tacos are a hit so don't come late expecting there to be any left to order. Cactus is the other item that runs out. -This is very casual and rather tiny place with just a handful of tables and chairs so be ready to do an order to go. text: Spent a Sunday evening at The Lark. - I highly recommend reservations, even on a Sunday night.We were greeted and seated promptly. The wait staff was very attentive and informative. Our EATS!!! Brussels Sprouts - full of flavor, I would say the portion is big enough for 4 people to split if you are having another "starter". For two people it was a little big (but not complaining). Central Coast Vegetable - this came as a salad with a poached egg on top. Citrus mixed with greens, and the creamy egg!! It was delicious! It would be a "reorder" for us. Spanish Octopus - OMG, this was a great order. The Octopus was cooked perfectly. Not to rubbery, full of flavor, great texture. The size was perfect for two people to split Smoked Pork Belly - This dish came out after all the above. It was ok. We should not have ordered it. We were stuffed after the other dishes. It was good, but honestly it seemed like the same pork belly dish you get all over town. Its good, but I rather have the Octopus or try something new. Cocktails - El Topo (I recommend asking for it to come with broken ice and not the one large cube) Nice and refreshing, would order again. Ambiance - tad loud if you're going for a nice quite romantic dinner. The atmosphere is great. Its lively, full of good music, and energy. The layout is open and airy, which is perfect on a summer night. Tables inside are set close together. I don't mind that style, plus you get to check out others dishes! I felt the portion for price was of value. Nothing seemed over the top expenses and the portions were decent. I would come back in a heart beat and maybe save room for one of the amazing desserts!

text: I brought my 12 year old son to Premier last week after a baseball injury. He hurt his hand and we thought his pinky finger was broken. We were checked in quickly. The receptionist was very friendly, as was the rest of the staff. My son had his hand x-rayed. The Physician's Assistant came into the room to tell us that my son had definitely broken his finger. He sent us on our way, X-ray pics on a disc, with instructions to follow up with an orthopedic surgeon. A few days later, we finally got to see the orthopedic hand surgeon at Children's Hospital. Imagine our surprise when we were told by the surgeon that my son's finger was not broken. According to the doctor, the X-ray quality was poor and there was a shadow that was misdiagnosed as a break. My son had a severe sprain with a hematoma and he will recover completely. While I was thrilled to get such great news I was really upset at the quality of care my son received. X-ray technicians are trained to know if the picture is one of good quality. How many times have you had an X-ray done and the tech says "let me make sure the pictures are ok before I let you go?" Additionally, the PA who was reading the X-rays should know when he's reading a poor quality scan. Thankfully, our issue was minor. If the providers at Premier can't diagnose a simple problem, how can anyone expect them to deal with things that require actual critical thinking skills? We won't be going back here again.
